functions.name: StaticFunction::operator()
functions.signature:
template <typename F, F *f>
template <typename... Ts>
auto StaticFunction<F, f>::operator()(Ts&&... args) const -> decltype(f(std::forward<Ts>(args)...))
functions.description: Invokes the bound static function pointer f with perfectly-forwarded arguments. This call operator adapts a compile-time function pointer (template parameter f) into a callable object. Typical usage: instantiate StaticFunction with a function type F and pointer f, then call the instance like a normal function; arguments are forwarded and the return type matches f’s return type.
requirements: Template parameter F must be a function type (e.g., R(Args...)).
Template non-type parameter f must be a valid pointer to a function of type F and must have external linkage.
The argument pack Ts... must make f(Ts&&...) a valid expression (i.e., f must be invocable with the provided arguments).
Any exceptions thrown by f will propagate to the caller; no internal error handling is performed.
If f has preconditions, the caller must satisfy them before invocation (not enforced here).

functions.name: util::GetTimeStamp
functions.description: Returns the current system_clock timestamp converted to the specified std::chrono duration, as the count of ticks since the Unix epoch. Intended for retrieving wall-clock time in various precisions (e.g., seconds, milliseconds, microseconds) by choosing Duration.
requirements: Template parameter Duration must be a std::chrono::duration type (e.g., std::chrono::seconds, std::chrono::milliseconds).
The return type is the underlying representation type Duration::rep (auto-deduced); callers should handle the potentially large integer-like value.
Based on std::chrono::system_clock; the value is wall-clock time and is not monotonic (can move backwards/forwards if the system time is adjusted).

functions.name: util::GetTimeStampMS
functions.description: Returns the current system_clock timestamp in milliseconds since the Unix epoch as an unsigned 64-bit integer. Convenience wrapper around util::GetTimeStamp<std::chrono::milliseconds>().
requirements: Returns wall-clock time from std::chrono::system_clock and is not guaranteed to be monotonic.

functions.name: util::GetTimeStampUS
functions.description: Returns the current system_clock timestamp in microseconds since the Unix epoch as an unsigned 64-bit integer. Convenience wrapper around util::GetTimeStamp<std::chrono::microseconds>().
requirements: Returns wall-clock time from std::chrono::system_clock and is not guaranteed to be monotonic.

unharnessable_functions.name: StaticFunction::operator()
unharnessable_functions.reason: This templated call operator requires a compile-time function type and non-type function pointer parameter; without a concrete instantiation (F and f) it cannot be meaningfully invoked by the fuzzer at runtime.
